bugs.error_message: PR #164 CI failed: cargo-deny 'error[vulnerability]: TLS 1.3 handshake messages incorrectly accepted across encryption level boundaries' (RUSTSEC-2026-0285) and Security Vulnerability Scan (cargo audit) exit 1 on the same advisory
bugs.root_cause: Cargo.lock pinned rustls v0.23.44 (transitive: kube client -> hyper-rustls -> rustls), which is below the RUSTSEC-2026-0285 / GHSA-2mjx-qc3c-rqvc fix version 0.23.45
bugs.fix: cargo update -p rustls (0.23.44 -> 0.23.45, lockfile-only); verified with `cargo deny check advisories` -> ok; changelog entry added

bugs.error_message: Dependabot PRs #173/#174 failed all CodeQL jobs: "Loaded a configuration file for version '4.38.1', but running version '4.38.0'"
bugs.root_cause: codeql-action monorepo sub-actions (init/analyze/upload-sarif) are distinct dependency names; the dependabot.yml group pattern 'github/codeql-action' matched none of them, so the family split into three PRs and any single bump mismatches init vs analyze
bugs.fix: re-pinned all six github/codeql-action/* refs to v4.38.1 (1c5b675) in one change across codeql/sast/scorecard/build workflows; added 'github/codeql-action/*' to the actions-routine group so the family bumps as one PR

bugs.error_message: PR #175 kind job: setup_file failed at `out=$(patch_annotation ...)` right after the admission policy applied; 'bats warning: Executed 1 instead of expected 5 tests'
bugs.root_cause: bats executes setup_file with errexit; the activation poll's probe patch exits non-zero exactly when the policy starts denying (the success condition), so the awaited denial aborted the file at the assignment
bugs.fix: append `|| true` to the probe assignment (comment marks it load-bearing); all other patch_annotation call sites already use bats `run`

bugs.error_message: PR #175 kind job round five: setup passes, then tests 1/2 fail the message assertion and tests 4/5 fail their allow assertion; only test 3 passes
bugs.root_cause: patch_annotation interpolated the value into the patch JSON unescaped; JSON-shaped values like {"namespace":"x"} broke the patch document, so kubectl exited non-zero with a PARSE error before any request — deny tests saw the wrong message, allow tests saw a failure; quote-free values (probe-N, deadbeef) worked, masking it in setup and test 3
bugs.fix: escape embedded quotes in the value (${value//\"/\\\"}) before building the -p document; verified unescaped form fails json.load and escaped form round-trips

bugs.error_message: ScheduledCapacity controller re-patched its own status on every reconcile, re-triggering its own watch: ~50 resourceVersion bumps/sec and a single handback timeout counted 100 times in the Prometheus counter.
bugs.root_cause: Three compounding mistakes in patch_status. (1) Condition::new() stamps lastTransitionTime with Utc::now(), so the computed condition set never equalled the stored one and every reconcile wrote. (2) There was no no-op guard comparing the computed status against the stored one before patching. (3) record_decision_metrics incremented the handback-timeout counter once per reconcile instead of once per transition into the phase. A later rewrite then introduced a fourth: build_status_value silently dropped the targetRef and spotSchedule keys, so the new no-op guard compared a desired status that could never equal the stored one and was permanently disabled, with no test failure and no visible symptom.
bugs.fix: merge_condition_timestamps() preserves each condition's lastTransitionTime unless its `status` actually changed (matched by type, not position); spot_schedule_transition_time() does the same for the mirrored provider timestamp. patch_status() deserialises the computed status into ScheduledCapacityStatus and returns early when it equals the stored one. record_decision_metrics() gates on entered_phase(). build_status_value() always emits every key the controller owns, using explicit JSON null for cleared fields (an omitted key in a merge patch leaves the stored value, so handbackDeadline could never be cleared). Guarded by test_build_status_value_emits_every_field_of_the_status_type, which derives the expected key set from a fully-populated ScheduledCapacityStatus rather than a hand-written list.
bugs.lesson: A controller that logs nothing on a successful reconcile cannot be debugged: the missing-success-log made a working watch look dead and sent the first diagnosis in the wrong direction. Always log reconcile completion. And any status field built by hand must be checked against the type, not against memory.

bugs.error_message: Machine create rejected by Cluster API v1.14.3: 'Machine in version "v1beta2" cannot be handled as a Machine: strict decoding error: unknown field "spec.bootstrap.configRef.apiVersion", unknown field "spec.bootstrap.configRef.namespace", unknown field "spec.infrastructureRef.apiVersion", unknown field "spec.infrastructureRef.namespace"'
bugs.root_cause: Only half of the CAPI version-agnostic design was implemented. resolve_capi_machine_version() discovered the served Machine version correctly (v1beta2 on CAPI v1.11+), but add_machine_to_cluster built spec.bootstrap.configRef and spec.infrastructureRef in exactly one shape: the v1beta1 core ObjectReference with apiVersion + namespace. v1beta2 replaced both with a ContractVersionedObjectReference whose only fields are apiGroup, kind and name, and the Machine type decodes strictly, so the surplus fields are a hard BadRequest rather than being pruned. It survived review because machine_api_version_for() passes the user's bootstrapSpec version through, so a ScheduledMachine declaring bootstrap.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1 produced a self-consistent v1beta1 Machine that the conversion webhook accepted; only a v1beta2 spec or the discovery fallback reached the bug, and every unit fixture assumes v1beta1.
bugs.fix: machine_contract_ref() in src/reconcilers/helpers.rs is now the only place either shape is written, keyed on uses_legacy_object_reference() against CAPI_LEGACY_OBJECT_REFERENCE_VERSIONS (v1alpha3, v1alpha4, v1beta1) in src/constants.rs. An unrecognised version resolves to the MODERN shape, since the legacy one is being removed. Six tests in helpers_tests.rs pin both shapes, the group derivation (version segment dropped) and the unknown-version default. ADR 0017. Verified live: Machine stored at cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta2 with apiGroup-form refs, phase Running, Node Ready.
bugs.lesson: Discovering a version is not the same as honouring its contract. When a controller branches on a discovered API version, every field whose SHAPE changed with that version has to branch too, and a unit suite whose fixtures all pin the old version cannot tell you otherwise. A passthrough default (here: the user's bootstrapSpec version) can keep the common path self-consistent and hide the bug on exactly the path that is the future.

bugs.error_message: Controller's Machine and Node secondary watches matched nothing: watch issued with labelSelector=5spot.eribourg.dev%2Fscheduled-machine while every created Machine was stamped 5spot.finos.org/scheduled-machine. Machine/Node state changes never triggered a reconcile of the owning ScheduledMachine.
bugs.root_cause: The API group rename from 5spot.eribourg.dev to 5spot.finos.org never reached src/labels.rs. Two constants described the same key: constants::SCHEDULED_MACHINE_LABEL (finos), which merge_owned_labels() STAMPS on every Machine, bootstrap and infra resource, and labels::LABEL_SCHEDULED_MACHINE (eribourg), which main.rs SELECTS on for both secondary watches and which machine_to_scheduled_machine()/node_to_scheduled_machines_via_machine() read. Security consequence: RESERVED_LABEL_PREFIXES covers 5spot.finos.org/ but not the retired domain, so the one key the reverse mapping trusted was injectable through machineTemplate.labels. An existing test had enshrined the bug, asserting that the canonical 5spot.finos.org key was an 'imposter'.
bugs.fix: labels::LABEL_SCHEDULED_MACHINE is now an alias of constants::SCHEDULED_MACHINE_LABEL, so the stamped key and the watched key are one definition and cannot drift; the five other 5-Spot label constants move to 5spot.finos.org. Three drift guards in labels_tests.rs (alias holds, no key on the retired group, owned key covered by RESERVED_LABEL_PREFIXES). test_machine_to_sm_wrong_prefix_label_is_ignored rewritten to use genuinely foreign prefixes and to assert the retired group no longer resolves. Threat model 1.7: T2's mitigation marked incomplete for that period, new T12 for tracking-label confusion.
bugs.lesson: Two string literals for one key will drift, and a label used on BOTH the write and the read side is the worst place for it: nothing fails, the watch just silently matches nothing, so the controller degrades from event-driven to timer-driven with no error anywhere. Alias the one constant instead of repeating the string. Also: a test asserting that the CORRECT value is wrong is the loudest possible signal that a rename was left half-finished, so when a test calls something an imposter, check which side is actually canonical.

bugs.error_message: Watch events reached the controller minutes late: a ScheduledMachine created at 00:41:41 was first reconciled at 00:44:22. Every watch failed on a fixed cadence (the ScheduledMachine reflector every 30s exactly) with 'ServiceError: error reading a body from connection' / hyper Body TimedOut, logged as 'kube-runtime will reconnect'.
bugs.root_cause: src/main.rs and src/reconcilers/child_client.rs set read_timeout = K8S_API_TIMEOUT_SECS (30s) on the shared kube Client for NIST SC-5, and every watch used watcher::Config::default(), whose server-side timeoutSeconds is 290. read_timeout is an idle timeout on every connection, watches included, so any watch with 30 quiet seconds was killed client-side; the reflector then backed off and events waited for the next relist. kube-runtime's contract is that the watch timeout must be lower than the client read timeout (kube-client 4.2 defaults read_timeout to None for exactly this reason). Present since the first commit. Misdiagnosed on 2026-10-09 as routine churn, and the 'demote to debug' change made on 2026-10-13 classed WatchFailed as routine, which would have hidden it.
bugs.fix: stream::watch_config() sets the server-side timeout to constants::WATCH_TIMEOUT_SECS (20s, with WATCH_TIMEOUT_MARGIN_SECS=10 under the 30s read timeout), and all 12 watch sites use it, so the apiserver closes each watch cleanly first and kube-runtime resumes from the last resourceVersion. Compile-time guards in constants.rs fail the build if the inequality is broken or the timeout is zero. is_routine_watch_restart() no longer treats WatchFailed as routine: a healthy watch never produces one. Tests in stream_tests.rs pin the config and the classification.
bugs.lesson: A symptom that recurs on a fixed cadence is a timer, not churn. 'Several times a minute on a healthy cluster' was the evidence for the defect and was read as the evidence against it. Before classifying a recurring error as routine, find the clock that produces it. Only a tier with a real apiserver and real timing (ADR 0019) could see the delay.

bugs.error_message: cargo-deny (License + Advisory + Sources) and Security Vulnerability Scan (cargo audit) failed on main: RUSTSEC-2026-0346, -0347, -0348, -0349 against rustls 0.23.45.
bugs.root_cause: New upstream advisories against the transitive rustls 0.23.45 (via kube-client / hyper-rustls). Not a code change: the lockfile pinned an affected version when the advisories were published.
bugs.fix: cargo update -p rustls --precise 0.23.46 (patched for all four). Lockfile-only diff; deny and audit clean afterwards.
bugs.lesson: An advisory failure on a branch that changed no dependencies is a new advisory, not a regression in the branch. Check which crate and which patched version, update only that crate with --precise, and confirm the lockfile diff is that crate alone. cargo-deny takes --all-features BEFORE the subcommand: `cargo deny --all-features check`; after `check` it is an argument error (exit 2) that looks like a failed check.

bugs.error_message: The shipped reclaim agent cannot run on Linux: with RECLAIM_DETECTOR unset, `auto` picks netlink, Subscriber::new() fails with ECONNREFUSED (os error 111), the agent exits, and the DaemonSet crash-loops. Emergency reclaim never worked out of the box.
bugs.root_cause: The kernel's proc connector delivers only to the initial network namespace. Measured with tests/integration_netlink_proc.rs as root: passes in the host netns, fails in `unshare -n`. Agent pods have their own netns, and the agent pod-security VAP denies hostNetwork (ADR 0004), so netlink could never open. The only netlink test runs by hand as root in the host namespace, the one case that works.
bugs.fix: ADR 0021: DetectorFlag::resolve_with probes netlink once for `auto` and falls back to poll with a warning; explicit netlink/poll are not probed. The DaemonSet sets RECLAIM_DETECTOR=poll and drops NET_ADMIN; VAP rule 7 admits no capability adds; the KSV-0022 trivyignore suppression is removed.
bugs.lesson: A test that only runs in the one environment where a feature works proves nothing about where it is deployed. Run the privileged/kernel-facing path in the namespace and policy context the pod actually gets.

bugs.error_message: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy 5spot-agent-pod-security denied the shipped kata-config agent DaemonSet pod: 'the kata config agent may only mount hostPath /'. The agent could not start on any cluster with the policy installed.
bugs.root_cause: ADR 0005 removed the configurable destPath and narrowed the DaemonSet's hostPath from / to /etc/k0s, but rule 6b of the agent pod-security policy still required '/' and its comment still described destPath. Nothing tested that the shipped agent pods pass their own policy.
bugs.fix: Rule 6b now admits exactly hostPath /etc/k0s (tighter than before). New .github/scripts/agent-pod-security.bats renders both shipped DaemonSets into Pods and asserts they are admitted, plus the denials (NET_ADMIN, any capability add, host-root mount).
bugs.lesson: A policy needs a positive test built from the real manifest it governs, not only deny tests: a correct-looking policy can block the very component it exists to allow.

bugs.error_message: deploy/node-agent/daemonset.yaml had two `args:` keys on the agent container after ADR 0020's manifest edit: `args: [agent, reclaim]` plus the existing `args: [--proc-root=/host/proc]`. YAML keeps the last, so the pod would run `5spot --proc-root=/host/proc`, the controller with an unknown flag.
bugs.root_cause: The ADR 0020 edit inserted a new args key above an existing one, and the check used yaml.safe_load, which silently accepts duplicate keys. CI passed because no tier deployed the reclaim agent.
bugs.fix: One args list: [agent, reclaim, --proc-root=/host/proc]. A strict duplicate-key check over deploy/ and examples/ added to validate-examples.py.
bugs.lesson: PyYAML's safe_load accepts duplicate mapping keys; validate manifests with a loader that rejects them. Before adding a key to a manifest block, look for that key further down the same block.

bugs.error_message: The capacity controller Deployment never became Ready: both pods Running 0/1, `kubectl rollout status deployment/5spot-capacity-controller` hung ('1 old replicas are pending termination').
bugs.root_cause: src/cmd/capacity_controller.rs called HealthState::set_k8s_connected(true) but never set_ready(true); /readyz requires both, so it answered 503 forever. Never noticed because no tier ever deployed the capacity controller from an image (the Dockerfiles did not even ship its binary before ADR 0020), and capacity-e2e.bats never ran in CI.
bugs.fix: startup_health_state() returns a connected and ready HealthState, served by the capacity controller; test_startup_health_state_is_ready pins it. The k0smotron e2e tier now deploys the capacity controller and runs capacity-e2e.bats.
bugs.lesson: Every binary that exposes /readyz needs a test that its startup path reports ready; a probe that can never pass is invisible until something waits on it.

bugs.error_message: Reclaim agent matched the process (pid 6736, pattern e2ereclaim) then exited: 'patch Node/e2e-reclaim: Failed to build request: failed to validate request: PatchParams::force only works with Patch::Apply'. CrashLoopBackOff; the Node was never annotated.
bugs.root_cause: annotate_node used PatchParams::apply(FIELD_MANAGER).force() with Patch::Merge. kube refuses force for anything but server-side apply, client-side, before sending. Every match in every detector mode failed, so emergency reclaim could never have worked. Unit tests covered the patch body, not the request; nothing ran the agent against an API server.
bugs.fix: annotation_patch_params(): a merge patch with the agent's field manager and no force. Tests go through kube's public Request::patch builder (the same validation): the agent's params pass, and the old forced-merge pairing is pinned as rejected.
bugs.lesson: A mocked API cannot catch a request the client library refuses to build. Test request construction through the library's own builder, and run node agents against a real API server.

bugs.error_message: capacity-e2e test 15 'a capacity field naming a reserved root is rejected': patching spec.capacity.field to metadata.ownerReferences succeeded (status 0).
bugs.root_cause: The CRD pattern for capacity.field checks only charset and depth; nothing at admission refused a reserved first segment (spec, metadata, status). Only the reconciler did, via error_policy, into its logs on every requeue. The concept doc, threat model §7 and CapacityError::Path rustdoc all claimed admission refused it. Not a security gap: the path is rooted at the owned object's spec.
bugs.fix: capacity_field_schema adds a CEL rule !self.matches('^(spec|metadata|status)([.]|$)') generated from the new constants::CAPACITY_FIELD_RESERVED_ROOTS, shared with capacity_path.rs. Verified on a v1.37 API server; capacity e2e 16/16.
bugs.lesson: When docs say 'enforced at admission', test it against a real API server: a schema pattern that cannot express the rule (RE2, no lookahead) silently leaves it to the reconciler. Use a CEL rule built from the same constant.
